## Motivation

- The DSV4 indexer sizes its paged gather and logits buffer from `MAX_SEQ_LEN_FOR_CAPTURE`. On `intel_dev` that is the full configured context. At `--context-length 262144 --page-size 256` it is 262148, because the pool adds padding (`deepseek_v4_backend.py:558`).
- Graph capture freezes that width. So a short conversation does full-context indexer work on every decode step.
- CUDA has the same cost: #40441 measured 2.68x faster per-request decode at `--context-length 131072` than at 1048576 (8x H200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark).

## Modifications

- **Opt-in widths, XPU only.** `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS` (default empty, so off) lists narrower capture widths. On a device other than XPU, a non-empty value raises an error (`deepseek_v4_backend.py:509`).
- **One graph per width.** The backend advertises the widths and always appends the full context as the last width. The runner captures one graph per width and replays the smallest width that fits the batch. The graph key carries the width. The shared runner code names no backend.
- **Bad combinations fail at startup.** `validate_deepseek_v4_decode_graph_widths` (`deepseek_v4_hook.py:198`) rejects the variable together with any of these:
  - speculative decoding (`speculative_algorithm`)
  - diffusion decoding (`dllm_algorithm`)
  - two-batch overlap (`enable_two_batch_overlap`)
  - PDMux (`enable_pdmux`)
  - a decode graph backend other than `full`
- **Eager forward passes use the full context.** A narrowed width belongs to a graph replay only. Since 2340f8c401, eager decode metadata uses the full context (`deepseek_v4_backend.py:1465`). At 3c0dbe0052, it could use the width of the last replay. Then a long eager batch would lose its trailing pages.
- **Off means unchanged.** With the variable unset, the runner captures one graph per batch size, with the same graph keys as before. `AttentionBackend` and `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` carry class-level `None` defaults. So the draft runners that skip `super().__init__()` still work.
- **The XPU gate stays.** I did not measure this code on CUDA. I think a device-neutral version belongs on `main`, based on #38993.

## Accuracy Tests

| file | result at 2340f8c401 (CPU) |
| --- | --- |
| `test_decode_cuda_graph_widths.py` (new) | 27 passed |
| `test_decode_cuda_graph_widths_spec_runners.py` (new) | 9 passed |
| `test_deepseek_v4.py` (adapted) | 10 passed, 8 skipped (need CUDA). The run uses an `sgl_kernel` import stub. This CPU host needs the stub at the base commit too. |

- The tests cover:
  - the width resolver, and width selection at the boundaries
  - the unchanged path with the variable unset
  - the full-context bound of eager decode
  - the graph keys, the validator and the draft runners
- The eager-path regression test fails at 3c0dbe0052 (`8192 != 262148`) and passes now.
- No accuracy run checked this PR. I expect no change in model output. The widths change how much the indexer scans, and the last width is always the full context.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x Arc Pro B70, TP8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, context length 262144. In each table, the width setting is the only difference between the rows.

**This PR's code (first revision), 1024 in / 1024 out, 1 user, 3 runs per row:**

| widths | tok/s per user | inter-token latency (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| off | 40.71 | 24.57 |
| `8192,32768` | 46.57 (+14.4%) | 21.47 (-12.6%) |

**A newer local build (2026-10-12), not this PR's code.** The build has local XPU changes that are not upstream yet. Two of them matter here:
- an earlier local version of this feature, which sets the same widths through another variable
- an indexer early exit: the indexer logits kernel stops at the length of each sequence, not at the longest sequence of the batch

Each figure is the mean of 2 launches:

| widths | 1k/1k, 1 user (tok/s per user) | 8k/512, 8 users (tok/s per user) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| off | 62.20 | 27.03 |
| `8192,32768` | 65.86 (+5.9%) | 28.66 (+6.1%) |

Each added graph costs about 0.42 s of capture time. Each added width keeps about 5 MB of device memory per rank. `max_total_num_tokens` changed by no more than one page (256 tokens) of jitter.

## Limits

- I found the eager-path defect by reading the code. No device run checked the fix.
- I measured this PR's code at 1024 in / 1024 out only. The gain should shrink as prompts grow toward the full context.
- I want a second opinion on one point. `can_run_graph` builds its graph key with the width label of the previous replay (`decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:526`). I found no wrong replay, because capture records every batch size x width combination.
- CI does not run on this PR, for three reasons:
  - The PR has no `run-ci` label.
  - The XPU lane runs only for pull requests to `main`.
  - The maintenance gate (#21065) blocks `intel_dev`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The feature is an environment variable with no doc page yet.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

We should consider this for not only xpu, to make it fully ready to upstream.
Thus do we know why cuda graph does not need such changes?  @inteljerry 

cc @CaoE  could you also help take a look?

One concern is the memory overhead introduced by adding multiple context-width variants. Since the full-context graph is still captured, configuring additional widths adds more graphs rather than replacing the original one. Because graph count scales roughly with batch_size × width_variants × other variants, this could increase both capture time and persistent device memory usage.

On memory-constrained devices, could this reduce the available KV-cache capacity, max_total_num_tokens, or max_running_requests, or even cause graph capture to fail with OOM? The PR reports decode performance improvements, but it would be helpful to include measurements of the additional memory usage and its impact on maximum context capacity and concurrency, comparing the default configuration with one or more width configurations.

Another concern is that this PR modifies the shared decode CUDA graph runner, which is used by multiple devices. Although the new logic is intended to be inactive when decode_graph_widths is unset, do we need to add regression coverage to verify that the existing capture and replay behavior remains unchanged for backends that do not advertise width variants ?

Thanks all for the comments!

**@jianan-gu on scope.** Agreed this should not stay XPU-only, and I do not have evidence that CUDA is unaffected. The mechanism is shared code: `MAX_SEQ_LEN_FOR_CAPTURE` feeds `make_core_attn_metadata(max_seq_len=...)` and on into `BuildPageTablePositions.execute(...)`, which sizes the page-table and paged-gather buffers, and capture then freezes that width for every replay. Nothing in that chain is XPU-specific.

The plumbing is already backend-neutral: the lines this PR adds to `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py` carry no XPU, DSV4 or DeepSeek reference, and a backend opts in purely by advertising `decode_graph_widths`. The restriction is one guard, at `deepseek_v4_backend.py:508`. So the gate reflects where I could measure — +13.4% tok/s/user and 11.8% lower ITL at 1024/1024, concurrency 1, on 8xB70 — rather than a claim about CUDA. I will try to run the same A/B test on Nvidia GPU(s). If the effect reproduces I would rather relax that guard in this PR than leave it as a follow-up; if it does not, the gate stays and I will say so here either way. If anyone already has a box free and gets there first, I am glad to take their numbers instead.

**@CaoE and @unrahul on memory.** The KV half is settled in source, and @unrahul's reading matches mine with one addition: `post_capture_kv_sizing_planned()` returns False three separate ways for this configuration — `device != "cuda"`, MLA enabled, and `is_deepseek_v4(hf_config)`. So the KV budget is sized from free memory and `mem_fraction_static` before capture with no graph term, and `max_total_num_tokens` cannot move.

The capture-headroom half is a fair question. `reserve_for_graph_mb()` adds `max_bs * 2` MB with no width term, so the reserve stays flat while graph count multiplies by the number of widths. The one thing that softens it is that the added graphs are the narrow ones, whose page-table and logits buffers are smaller than the full-context graph already being captured, so the marginal cost per width sits below the existing one rather than equal to it. That is reasoning, not a number.

**Two things I will do.**

1. @unrahul's three-arm experiment: one image, one source tree, identical arguments, changing only the variable — unset, then `8192,32768`, then `8192,32768,65536` — reporting `max_total_num_tokens`, capture wall time and peak memory during capture for each arm. I will post the table here.

2. @CaoE's coverage point, which is a real gap rather than a covered one. The current tests pin the pure helpers with the feature off: the resolver returns `()` for an empty configuration, and `_compose_graph_width_variant("lora", None, 8192)` returns `"lora"` unchanged. What is missing is the runner itself with a backend that advertises nothing — that `capture_widths` collapses to `(None,)`, that `_make_graph_key` is identical to before, and that `can_run_graph` never consults the new check. The test helper always builds a runner with widths populated, so that path is genuinely untested. I will add those cases.

Experiment results are summarized below, including follow-ups for the two failure modes @CaoE raised: graph capture failing, and runtime OOM on workloads whose activation memory peaks near the limit. 
25 server launches on 8x Arc Pro B70, TP8. Same image, same source tree, same arguments, with `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS` as the only variable. Arms were run round-robin instead of one block per arm, so any drift over the hour is spread across all three.

Configuration: `--page-size 256 --context-length 262144 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --max-running-requests 8 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, decode graphs full at `bs=[1,2,4,8]`, prefill graphs disabled. `--max-total-tokens` is intentionally not passed, so the token budget is derived from free memory and can move between arms.

### @unrahul: the three experiments

3 repeats per arm, mean (min-max):

| metric | unset (4 graphs) | `8192,32768` (12) | `8192,32768,65536` (16) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_total_num_tokens` | 518912 (518656-519168) | 518827 (518656-519168) | 518997 (518656-519168) |
| capture elapsed, TP0 | 19.64 s (19.35-19.95) | 23.26 s (23.08-23.61) | 24.84 s (24.71-25.06) |
| capture retained, TP0 | 2.26 GB | 2.27 GB | 2.27 GB |
| capture retained, TP1-7 | 0.74 GB | 0.75 GB | 0.75 GB |
| free after capture, TP0 | 2.09 GB | 2.08 GB | 2.08 GB |
| time to ready | 100 s | 105 s | 108 s |

`max_total_num_tokens` covers the same range in all three arms and the means are non-monotonic in graph count, so there is no arm effect above a one-page (256 token) jitter.

TP0 is quoted throughout because it is the binding rank: it retains roughly 3x what TP1-7 do (2.26 vs 0.74 GB). An 8-rank average would report 0.93 GB and understate the worst rank by 2.4x.

Resolved ladders, taken from each arm's own log: `(8192, 32768, 262148)` and `(8192, 32768, 65536, 262148)`.

### Establishing a slope for the memory cost

The memory deltas above sit at the log's resolution. `mem usage` prints GB to two decimals, so 0.01 GB is one least-significant digit, and at 12 and 16 graphs that is the entire delta. Three points at the resolution floor do not determine a slope, so longer ladders were captured:

| widths | graphs | retained TP0 | capture elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 2.26 GB | 20.01 s |
| 4 | 16 | 2.27 GB | 24.84 s |
| 6 | 24 | 2.28 GB | 29.19 s |
| 7 | 28 | 2.29 GB | 30.08 s |

That is 0.03 GB across six added widths, or approximately **5 MB of retained device memory per added width, per rank**. Capture time is 10.1 s across 24 added graphs, or **0.42 s per added graph**, which agrees with the marginals computed independently from the three-arm table above (0.45 and 0.40 s/graph).

For scale, the 4-graph baseline retains 2.26 GB on TP0, so each additional rung adds roughly 0.2% on top of it.

### @CaoE: can graph capture fail?
Capture failure is determined by the peak, so the cliff was measured directly by raising `--mem-fraction-static` until capture breaks:

| `mem_fraction_static` | `max_total_num_tokens` | free at capture begin | unset | 4 rungs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.85 | ~518,000 | 4.53 GB | ready | ready |
| 0.89 | ~686,000 | 3.31 GB | ready | ready |
| 0.93 | ~854,000 | 2.09 GB | ready, 0.02 GB free after | ready, 0.02 GB free after |

At 0.93 the binding rank completes capture with 20 MB remaining, and the 4-rung ladder survives the same point. It retained slightly less there than the baseline (1.89 vs 1.90 GB) and obtained marginally more KV tokens (854,528 vs 853,760), so the difference is below run-to-run variation even at the edge.

The pool appears to size itself against available memory instead of requesting a fixed amount: TP0 retained 2.26 GB at 0.85 but 1.90 GB at 0.93 for the same four graphs. Additional graphs are absorbed into the same budget, and the cost surfaces as capture time.

### @CaoE: can activation peaks cause a runtime OOM?

Concurrency 8 (= `max_running_requests`), 8000-token inputs, sampling all eight devices for the duration of the run:

| arm | peak device memory | peak util | min free | tok/s/user |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unset | 32655 MiB | 100.0% | 3 MiB | 17.67 |
| `8192,32768` | 32655 MiB | 100.0% | 3 MiB | 25.17 |
| `8192,32768,65536` | 32655 MiB | 100.0% | 3 MiB | 25.31 |

The peak is identical across all three arms, and the arm with the feature disabled already reaches 100%. The KV pool is sized from free memory so that it fills the device, so 100% is the expected steady state here and not a consequence of this change.

One limit on that measurement: at 100% with 3 MiB free it cannot resolve a 5-30 MB difference. It establishes that the ladder does not raise the peak. It cannot determine whether it consumes a small amount of slack, because no arm has any.

The activation ceiling in this configuration is set by `chunked_prefill_size` and `max_prefill_tokens`, and prefill graphs are disabled so prefill runs eagerly against those caps. This PR modifies neither, so the ladder shifts the floor by its retained cost and leaves the peak unchanged.



On lowering `mem_fraction_static` as a workaround: it does not appear necessary at this scale, since the configuration that barely survives with the feature disabled survives equally with four rungs. That holds for the shape measured here and should not be extrapolated further. If there is a specific memory-constrained configuration worth testing, the harness takes an argument list and the runs are inexpensive.

- The speed table now counts the measured requests, not the warmup request: 40.71 to 46.57 tok/s per user (+14.4%).
- On a newer local build, the same widths still give +5.9% (1k/1k, 1 user) and +6.1% (8k/512, 8 users). That build is not this PR's code. It sets the widths through an earlier local version of this feature. It also has a local indexer early exit, which stops the indexer logits at the length of each sequence.

- I did not run this code on CUDA. Upstream #40441 shows the same cost on 8x H200 with DSpark. There, per-request decode was 2.68x faster at 131K context than at 1M.

files.patch:
@@ -193,3 +193,48 @@ def validate_deepseek_v4_cp(server_args: ServerArgs) -> None:
         f"dp_size={server_args.dp_size}, moe_dense_tp_size={server_args.moe_dense_tp_size}, "
         f"attn_cp_size={server_args.attn_cp_size}, ep_size={server_args.ep_size}, tp_size={server_args.tp_size}"
     )
+
+
+def validate_deepseek_v4_decode_graph_widths(server_args: ServerArgs) -> None:
+    """Reject decode-graph capture widths alongside features that cannot serve them.
+
+    The widths narrow the DSV4 indexer's captured working width, which only
+    holds for plain decode graphs replayed from the full graph backend on a
+    single stream. Checking here means a bad combination fails while arguments
+    are still being resolved, rather than after a model has been built.
+    """
+    if not envs.SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS.get():
+        return
+
+    from sglang.srt.model_executor.cuda_graph_config import Backend
+
+    if server_args.speculative_algorithm:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS supports plain decode only; it "
+            "cannot be combined with speculative decoding "
+            f"({server_args.speculative_algorithm!r}). Unset one of them."
+        )
+    if server_args.dllm_algorithm is not None:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS supports plain decode only; it "
+            "cannot be combined with diffusion decoding "
+            f"({server_args.dllm_algorithm!r}). Unset one of them."
+        )
+    if server_args.enable_two_batch_overlap:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS does not support two-batch "
+            "overlap. The XPU graph runner rejects two-batch overlap, and the "
+            "overlap wrapper hides the capture widths from the runner. "
+            "Unset one of them."
+        )
+    if server_args.enable_pdmux:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS does not support PDMux. "
+            "Unset one of them."
+        )
+    if server_args.cuda_graph_config.decode.backend != Backend.FULL:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS requires the full decode graph "
+            f"backend, got {server_args.cuda_graph_config.decode.backend!r}. "

+    ``__init__`` of its own inherits its parent's verdict.
+    """
+    bases, own_init = {}, {}
+    for path in _SRT_ROOT.rglob("*.py"):
+        try:
+            source = path.read_text()
+        except UnicodeDecodeError:
+            continue
+        # Cheap pre-filter: only files naming some *GraphRunner can define a
+        # subclass in the family. Keeps whole-tree coverage without parsing
+        # ~1500 files that cannot contribute.
+        if _FILTER_TOKEN not in source:
+            continue
+        try:
+            tree = ast.parse(source)
+        except SyntaxError:
+            continue
+        for node in ast.walk(tree):
+            if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
+                continue
+            # Accept both `class X(Base)` and `class X(module.Base)`; a
+            # dotted base yields an ast.Attribute whose .attr is the class
+            # name. Dropping those would let a subclass declared that way
+            # escape the ratchet entirely.
+            bases[node.name] = [
+                b.id if isinstance(b, ast.Name) else b.attr
+                for b in node.bases
+                if isinstance(b, (ast.Name, ast.Attribute))
+            ]
+            own_init[node.name] = next(
+                (
+                    m
+                    for m in node.body
+                    if isinstance(m, ast.FunctionDef) and m.name == "__init__"
+                ),
+                None,
+            )
+
+    family = {DecodeCudaGraphRunner.__name__}
+    while True:
+        grown = {c for c, bs in bases.items() if family.intersection(bs)} - family
+        if not grown:
+            break
+        family |= grown
+
+    def skips_super(name, seen=()):
+        init = own_init.get(name)
+        if init is None:  # inherits one; follow the first base in the family
+            parents = [b for b in bases.get(name, []) if b in family and b not in seen]
+            return any(skips_super(p, (*seen, name)) for p in parents)
+        return not any(
+            isinstance(n, ast.Call)
+            and isinstance(n.func, ast.Attribute)
+            and n.func.attr == "__init__"
+            and isinstance(n.func.value, ast.Call)
+            and getattr(n.func.value.func, "id", None) == "super"
+            for n in ast.walk(init)
+        )
+
+    return {
+        name for name in family - {DecodeCudaGraphRunner.__name__} if skips_super(name)
+    }
+
+
+def _draft_runner(cls):
+    """Only the state a draft runner's own ``__init__`` would have set."""
+    runner = cls.__new__(cls)
+    runner.model_runner = SimpleNamespace(
+        device="cpu", gpu_id=0, model=object(), tp_group=None
+    )
+    runner.capture_bs = [1]
+    runner.compile_bs = set()
+    runner.captured_req_width = 1
+    runner.attn_backend = Mock()
+    runner.capture_one_shape = Mock()
+    return runner
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _capture_loop_isolated():
+    """Stub the device and compile plumbing so the loop body is observable."""
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def fake_patch_model(*_args, **_kwargs):
+        yield "forward"
+
+    with patch(f"{RUNNER_MOD}.get_available_gpu_memory", return_value=0.0), patch(
+        f"{RUNNER_MOD}.get_parallel", return_value=SimpleNamespace(tp_rank=1)
+    ), patch(
+        f"{RUNNER_MOD}.torch_compile_decoration.patch_model", fake_patch_model
+    ), patch(
+        f"{RUNNER_MOD}._set_capture_lora_variant"
+    ):
+        yield
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _without_class_defaults():
+    """Remove the defaults so a test can observe the original defect."""
+    saved = {name: DecodeCudaGraphRunner.__dict__[name] for name in WIDTH_ATTRS}
+    for name in WIDTH_ATTRS:
+        delattr(DecodeCudaGraphRunner, name)
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        for name, value in saved.items():
+            setattr(DecodeCudaGraphRunner, name, value)
+
+
+class TestDraftRunnersInheritWidthDefaults(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_base_class_carries_none_defaults(self):
+        # The base class owns them, so a fifth draft runner inherits them free.
+        for name in WIDTH_ATTRS:
+            with self.subTest(attr=name):
+                self.assertIn(name, DecodeCudaGraphRunner.__dict__)
+                self.assertIsNone(DecodeCudaGraphRunner.__dict__[name])
+
+    def test_both_attributes_resolve_on_an_instance_built_without_super(self):
+        # The capture loop needs decode_graph_widths; execute()'s replay log
+        # needs _active_decode_graph_width, and
+        # MultiLayerEagleDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner inherits execute rather
+        # than overriding it. Both must resolve on a runner that never ran the
+        # base __init__.
+        for cls in DRAFT_RUNNERS:
+            runner = cls.__new__(cls)
+            for name in WIDTH_ATTRS:
+                with self.subTest(runner=cls.__name__, attr=name):
+                    self.assertIsNone(getattr(runner, name))
+
+    def test_draft_runners_do_not_shadow_the_defaults(self):
+        # Assigning either name would opt the draft side into the ladder.
+        for cls in DRAFT_RUNNERS:
+            stores = _self_stores_anywhere(cls)
+            for name in WIDTH_ATTRS:
+                with self.subTest(runner=cls.__name__, attr=name):
+                    self.assertIsNone(inspect.getattr_static(cls, name))
+                    self.assertNotIn(name, stores)
+
+
+class TestExposedRunnerRatchet(CustomTestCase):
+    """Keep DRAFT_RUNNERS in step with the tree, in both directions.
+
+    A new runner that skips ``super().__init__()`` is exposed to this defect
+    class and the tests below would not cover it; a runner that starts calling
+    ``super().__init__()`` should leave the roster.
+    """
+
+    def test_roster_matches_the_source_tree(self):
+        pinned = {cls.__name__ for cls in DRAFT_RUNNERS}
+        discovered = _discover_exposed_runners()
+
+        grown = discovered - pinned
+        self.assertFalse(
+            grown,
+            f"{sorted(grown)} subclass DecodeCudaGraphRunner without calling "
+            "super().__init__(), so they inherit the capture path with only "
+            "part of its state. Add them to DRAFT_RUNNERS, or call "
+            "super().__init__().",
+        )
+        shrunk = pinned - discovered
+        self.assertFalse(
+            shrunk,
+            f"{sorted(shrunk)} no longer skip super().__init__(); drop them "
+            "from DRAFT_RUNNERS to lock in the progress.",
+        )
+
+
+class TestBackendCarriesTheDefault(CustomTestCase):
+    """The runner reads `self.attn_backend.decode_graph_widths` directly.
+
+    That read is only safe because every backend inherits the attribute. A
+    backend that never assigns it must still answer None rather than raise.
+    """
+
+    def test_a_backend_that_never_assigns_it_still_answers_none(self):
+        self.assertIn("decode_graph_widths", AttentionBackend.__dict__)
+        self.assertIsNone(AttentionBackend.__dict__["decode_graph_widths"])
+
+        class _BareBackend(AttentionBackend):
+            def __init__(self):
+                pass
+
+        self.assertIsNone(_BareBackend().decode_graph_widths)
+
+
+class TestDraftRunnerCaptureLoop(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_capture_loop_runs_and_never_narrows_the_draft_backend(self):
+        for cls in DRAFT_RUNNERS:
+            with self.subTest(runner=cls.__name__):
+                runner = _draft_runner(cls)
+                with _capture_loop_isolated():
+                    runner._capture_one_stream()
+
+                runner.capture_one_shape.assert_called_once_with(
+                    1, "forward", None, None
+                )
+                runner.attn_backend.set_decode_graph_width.assert_not_called()
+                self.assertIsNone(runner._active_decode_graph_width)
+
+    def test_capture_loop_fails_without_the_defaults(self):
+        # Control: if this stops failing, the test above guards nothing.
+        runner = _draft_runner(EAGLEDraftCudaGraphRunner)
+        with _without_class_defaults(), _capture_loop_isolated():
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(AttributeError, "decode_graph_widths"):
+                runner._capture_one_stream()
+
+    def test_draft_graph_keys_carry_no_width_even_with_a_ladder(self):
+        # Draft graphs are keyed by batch size alone, so two widths would
+        # collide. The base implementation would key "dsv4_seq=8192" here.
+        for cls in DRAFT_RUNNERS:
+            with self.subTest(runner=cls.__name__):
+                runner = _draft_runner(cls)
+                runner.decode_graph_widths = DecodeGraphWidths(
+                    widths=(8192, 262148), label="dsv4_seq"
+                )
+                runner._active_decode_graph_width = 8192
+                key = runner._make_graph_key(4)
+                self.assertEqual(key, ShapeKey(size=4))
+                self.assertIsNone(key.variant_label)
+
+
+class TestCaptureLoopReadsOnlyDraftProvidedState(CustomTestCase):
+    """Guard the defect class, not only the two attributes that hit it: a new
+    instance attribute set in the base ``__init__`` and read by
+    ``_capture_one_stream`` fails here rather than at capture on a server.
+    """
+
+    def test_every_read_is_resolvable_on_each_draft_runner(self):
+        reads = _self_attrs(DecodeCudaGraphRunner._capture_one_stream, ast.Load)
+        self.assertIn("decode_graph_widths", reads)  # the original crash site
+        for cls in DRAFT_RUNNERS:
+            assigned = _self_stores_anywhere(cls)
+            unresolved = {
+                name
+                for name in reads
+                if name not in assigned
+                and not callable(inspect.getattr_static(cls, name, None))
+                and not isinstance(inspect.getattr_static(cls, name, None), property)
+                and name not in DecodeCudaGraphRunner.__dict__
+            }
+            with self.subTest(runner=cls.__name__):
+                self.assertEqual(unresolved, set())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
We should consider this for not only xpu, to make it fully ready to upstream.
Thus do we know why cuda graph does not need such changes?  @inteljerry 

cc @CaoE  could you also help take a look?

One concern is the memory overhead introduced by adding multiple context-width variants. Since the full-context graph is still captured, configuring additional widths adds more graphs rather than replacing the original one. Because graph count scales roughly with batch_size × width_variants × other variants, this could increase both capture time and persistent device memory usage.

On memory-constrained devices, could this reduce the available KV-cache capacity, max_total_num_tokens, or max_running_requests, or even cause graph capture to fail with OOM? The PR reports decode performance improvements, but it would be helpful to include measurements of the additional memory usage and its impact on maximum context capacity and concurrency, comparing the default configuration with one or more width configurations.

Another concern is that this PR modifies the shared decode CUDA graph runner, which is used by multiple devices. Although the new logic is intended to be inactive when decode_graph_widths is unset, do we need to add regression coverage to verify that the existing capture and replay behavior remains unchanged for backends that do not advertise width variants ?

reviews.body:
Thanks all for the comments!

**@jianan-gu on scope.** Agreed this should not stay XPU-only, and I do not have evidence that CUDA is unaffected. The mechanism is shared code: `MAX_SEQ_LEN_FOR_CAPTURE` feeds `make_core_attn_metadata(max_seq_len=...)` and on into `BuildPageTablePositions.execute(...)`, which sizes the page-table and paged-gather buffers, and capture then freezes that width for every replay. Nothing in that chain is XPU-specific.

The plumbing is already backend-neutral: the lines this PR adds to `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py` carry no XPU, DSV4 or DeepSeek reference, and a backend opts in purely by advertising `decode_graph_widths`. The restriction is one guard, at `deepseek_v4_backend.py:508`. So the gate reflects where I could measure — +13.4% tok/s/user and 11.8% lower ITL at 1024/1024, concurrency 1, on 8xB70 — rather than a claim about CUDA. I will try to run the same A/B test on Nvidia GPU(s). If the effect reproduces I would rather relax that guard in this PR than leave it as a follow-up; if it does not, the gate stays and I will say so here either way. If anyone already has a box free and gets there first, I am glad to take their numbers instead.

**@CaoE and @unrahul on memory.** The KV half is settled in source, and @unrahul's reading matches mine with one addition: `post_capture_kv_sizing_planned()` returns False three separate ways for this configuration — `device != "cuda"`, MLA enabled, and `is_deepseek_v4(hf_config)`. So the KV budget is sized from free memory and `mem_fraction_static` before capture with no graph term, and `max_total_num_tokens` cannot move.

The capture-headroom half is a fair question. `reserve_for_graph_mb()` adds `max_bs * 2` MB with no width term, so the reserve stays flat while graph count multiplies by the number of widths. The one thing that softens it is that the added graphs are the narrow ones, whose page-table and logits buffers are smaller than the full-context graph already being captured, so the marginal cost per width sits below the existing one rather than equal to it. That is reasoning, not a number.

**Two things I will do.**

1. @unrahul's three-arm experiment: one image, one source tree, identical arguments, changing only the variable — unset, then `8192,32768`, then `8192,32768,65536` — reporting `max_total_num_tokens`, capture wall time and peak memory during capture for each arm. I will post the table here.

2. @CaoE's coverage point, which is a real gap rather than a covered one. The current tests pin the pure helpers with the feature off: the resolver returns `()` for an empty configuration, and `_compose_graph_width_variant("lora", None, 8192)` returns `"lora"` unchanged. What is missing is the runner itself with a backend that advertises nothing — that `capture_widths` collapses to `(None,)`, that `_make_graph_key` is identical to before, and that `can_run_graph` never consults the new check. The test helper always builds a runner with widths populated, so that path is genuinely untested. I will add those cases.

Experiment results are summarized below, including follow-ups for the two failure modes @CaoE raised: graph capture failing, and runtime OOM on workloads whose activation memory peaks near the limit. 
25 server launches on 8x Arc Pro B70, TP8. Same image, same source tree, same arguments, with `SGLANG_DSV4_DECODE_GRAPH_SEQ_LENS` as the only variable. Arms were run round-robin instead of one block per arm, so any drift over the hour is spread across all three.

Configuration: `--page-size 256 --context-length 262144 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --max-running-requests 8 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, decode graphs full at `bs=[1,2,4,8]`, prefill graphs disabled. `--max-total-tokens` is intentionally not passed, so the token budget is derived from free memory and can move between arms.

### @unrahul: the three experiments

3 repeats per arm, mean (min-max):

| metric | unset (4 graphs) | `8192,32768` (12) | `8192,32768,65536` (16) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_total_num_tokens` | 518912 (518656-519168) | 518827 (518656-519168) | 518997 (518656-519168) |
| capture elapsed, TP0 | 19.64 s (19.35-19.95) | 23.26 s (23.08-23.61) | 24.84 s (24.71-25.06) |
| capture retained, TP0 | 2.26 GB | 2.27 GB | 2.27 GB |
| capture retained, TP1-7 | 0.74 GB | 0.75 GB | 0.75 GB |
| free after capture, TP0 | 2.09 GB | 2.08 GB | 2.08 GB |
| time to ready | 100 s | 105 s | 108 s |

`max_total_num_tokens` covers the same range in all three arms and the means are non-monotonic in graph count, so there is no arm effect above a one-page (256 token) jitter.

TP0 is quoted throughout because it is the binding rank: it retains roughly 3x what TP1-7 do (2.26 vs 0.74 GB). An 8-rank average would report 0.93 GB and understate the worst rank by 2.4x.

Resolved ladders, taken from each arm's own log: `(8192, 32768, 262148)` and `(8192, 32768, 65536, 262148)`.

### Establishing a slope for the memory cost

The memory deltas above sit at the log's resolution. `mem usage` prints GB to two decimals, so 0.01 GB is one least-significant digit, and at 12 and 16 graphs that is the entire delta. Three points at the resolution floor do not determine a slope, so longer ladders were captured:

| widths | graphs | retained TP0 | capture elapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 2.26 GB | 20.01 s |
| 4 | 16 | 2.27 GB | 24.84 s |
| 6 | 24 | 2.28 GB | 29.19 s |
| 7 | 28 | 2.29 GB | 30.08 s |

That is 0.03 GB across six added widths, or approximately **5 MB of retained device memory per added width, per rank**. Capture time is 10.1 s across 24 added graphs, or **0.42 s per added graph**, which agrees with the marginals computed independently from the three-arm table above (0.45 and 0.40 s/graph).

For scale, the 4-graph baseline retains 2.26 GB on TP0, so each additional rung adds roughly 0.2% on top of it.

### @CaoE: can graph capture fail?
Capture failure is determined by the peak, so the cliff was measured directly by raising `--mem-fraction-static` until capture breaks:

| `mem_fraction_static` | `max_total_num_tokens` | free at capture begin | unset | 4 rungs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.85 | ~518,000 | 4.53 GB | ready | ready |
| 0.89 | ~686,000 | 3.31 GB | ready | ready |
| 0.93 | ~854,000 | 2.09 GB | ready, 0.02 GB free after | ready, 0.02 GB free after |

At 0.93 the binding rank completes capture with 20 MB remaining, and the 4-rung ladder survives the same point. It retained slightly less there than the baseline (1.89 vs 1.90 GB) and obtained marginally more KV tokens (854,528 vs 853,760), so the difference is below run-to-run variation even at the edge.

The pool appears to size itself against available memory instead of requesting a fixed amount: TP0 retained 2.26 GB at 0.85 but 1.90 GB at 0.93 for the same four graphs. Additional graphs are absorbed into the same budget, and the cost surfaces as capture time.

### @CaoE: can activation peaks cause a runtime OOM?

Concurrency 8 (= `max_running_requests`), 8000-token inputs, sampling all eight devices for the duration of the run:

| arm | peak device memory | peak util | min free | tok/s/user |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unset | 32655 MiB | 100.0% | 3 MiB | 17.67 |
| `8192,32768` | 32655 MiB | 100.0% | 3 MiB | 25.17 |
| `8192,32768,65536` | 32655 MiB | 100.0% | 3 MiB | 25.31 |

The peak is identical across all three arms, and the arm with the feature disabled already reaches 100%. The KV pool is sized from free memory so that it fills the device, so 100% is the expected steady state here and not a consequence of this change.

One limit on that measurement: at 100% with 3 MiB free it cannot resolve a 5-30 MB difference. It establishes that the ladder does not raise the peak. It cannot determine whether it consumes a small amount of slack, because no arm has any.

The activation ceiling in this configuration is set by `chunked_prefill_size` and `max_prefill_tokens`, and prefill graphs are disabled so prefill runs eagerly against those caps. This PR modifies neither, so the ladder shifts the floor by its retained cost and leaves the peak unchanged.



On lowering `mem_fraction_static` as a workaround: it does not appear necessary at this scale, since the configuration that barely survives with the feature disabled survives equally with four rungs. That holds for the shape measured here and should not be extrapolated further. If there is a specific memory-constrained configuration worth testing, the harness takes an argument list and the runs are inexpensive.
